# Where Arawn works now: the myths behind the markets

The myths did not retire. They moved offices. This is the file on where **Arawn** works now.

Arawn's whole dossier is one story, and it is the opening movement of the Mabinogi: the hunting-debt at Glyn Cuch and the year-long exchange that turns an insult into the strongest friendship in Welsh prose. Every word of it is preserved in the First Branch, Pwyll Pendefig Dyfed.

The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) — which maps every flagship temple to the industries its archetype demonstrably resonates with, each match argued and open to challenge — seats this temple in **3 industries**. This file reads those seats the way they were earned: through the myths.

## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Arawn
- **Pantheon:** Celtic
- **Domain of influence:** Otherworld, Annwn
- **Pattern seats:** 3
- **Sectors touched:** Commerce & Governance · Home & Lifestyle
- **Strongest seat:** Leadership, Governance & Public Administration
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 36 of 437

## The Myth at Work

**The Wrong at Glyn Cuch.** Pwyll, lord of Dyfed, goes hunting at Glyn Cuch, and there he sees a sight he has never seen: a pack of hounds shining white with red ears bringing down a stag.  He drives them off and sets his own hounds on the kill — and the stranger who rides up is Arawn, king of Annwn, and it was his hunt. — hold that image; the industries below are where it goes to work.

**The Exchange of Shapes.** Each king takes the other's form and goes to the other's court, and neither realm suspects.  Arawn rules Dyfed so well that there had never been so good a year in it. — remember the shape of that act. You will see it again, wearing a logo.

## The Seats

Each of these is argued in the atlas with a weight and a why-line. What the atlas cannot fit in one line is the whole myth — so here is each seat with its story restored.

### Leadership, Governance & Public Administration

*Government, executive leadership, and statecraft. (Sector: Commerce & Governance)*

The why-line says it in one breath: *The king whose honor holds when no one is watching — a year on another man's throne without a single trespass.* That is not a resemblance; it is the same act, performed in a newer building.

### Legal, Justice & Compliance

*Law, courts, and regulatory compliance. (Sector: Commerce & Governance)*

*The hunting-debt at Glyn Cuch and the single permitted blow at the ford — the Mabinogion's case study in honorable settlement.* — the atlas stops there, out of discipline. The myth keeps going: the function Arawn performs in the stories is precisely the function this industry sells.

### Pet Care & Animal Industries

*Pet products, veterinary care, and animal brands. (Sector: Home & Lifestyle)*

The why-line says it in one breath: *His white hounds with their red ears — the Otherworld pack.* That is not a resemblance; it is the same act, performed in a newer building.

## The Long Employment

Lady Charlotte Guest's translation of the Mabinogion (1838–49) carried Arawn out of the White and Red Books and into English, and the white red-eared hounds entered the stock of Celtic imagery from that day.  In the twentieth century the figure found his widest audience inverted: Lloyd Alexander's Chronicles of Prydain (1964–68) made 'Arawn Death-Lord of Annuvin' the arch-villain of five children's novels, and Disney's The Black Cauldron (1985) kept the dark-lord version on screen — a long way from the most honorable king in Welsh prose, but the reason the name is known worldwide. The age changed. The work did not.

## The Method, Stated Plainly

None of this is numerology. A seat exists only where the match can be argued from the deity’s documented domains and deeds — weighted, published, and falsifiable. ## For the Ones Who Work There

If you work in leadership, governance & public administration, legal, justice & compliance, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it. The [patron tier](/arawn/patron/) and the [advertising terms](/terms/advertising/) describe the mechanics; the resonance above describes the fit.
